UnitStatement: Deliverable DEL-00-02 (Repository and module boundary architecture) belongs to Package PKG-00 (Software Architecture Runway).
DEL-00-02 is of type API_CONTRACT.
DEL-00-02 has lifecycle target SEMANTIC_READY before downstream package-level work proceeds.
DEL-00-02 covers scope items SOW-057 and SOW-062 and objective OBJ-013.
Anticipated artifacts of DEL-00-02 are docs/architecture/module_boundaries.md and architecture dependency rules.
The write boundary of DEL-00-02 is limited to deliverable-local document kit and semantic artifacts only.
The purpose of DEL-00-02 is to define repository/module ownership boundaries and dependency direction before implementation.
DEL-00-02 defines architecture contracts only; it does not create modules, source files, build scripts, package manifests, or implementation code.
The architecture roles of DEL-00-02 include a layer map, a module ownership table, dependency direction rules, and an adapter governance boundary.
DEL-00-02 requires INIT.md as source basis for project bootstrap and data-boundary constraints.
DEL-00-02 requires docs/CONTRACT.md as source basis for invariants that must be preserved.
DEL-00-02 requires docs/SPEC.md as source basis for target software layers and architecture vocabulary.
DEL-00-02 requires execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 as authority for package and deliverable scope.
DEL-00-02 requires docs/_Registers/Deliverables.csv row DEL-00-02 for scope identity.
DEL-00-02 requires docs/_Registers/ScopeLedger.csv rows SOW-057 and SOW-062 for scope mapping.
DEL-00-02 requires execution/_Coordination/_COORDINATION.md for approved DAG-006 graph authority and SEMANTIC_READY architecture-basis handling.
Final repository layout names are a TBD human-ruling slot for DEL-00-02.
Monorepo versus package-manager selection is a TBD human-ruling slot for DEL-00-02.
Language-specific module syntax is a TBD human-ruling slot for DEL-00-02.
Lint tooling is a TBD human-ruling slot for DEL-00-02.
DEL-00-02 expects to output docs/architecture/module_boundaries.md.
DEL-00-02 expects to output architecture dependency rules.
No product implementation code is authorized by DEL-00-02.
DEL-00-02 introduces no protected standards text, standards tables, code-derived formulas, proprietary values, or vendor-private data.
DEL-00-02 architecture outputs remain draft/proposal material until accepted by the human project authority.
The DEL-00-02 work product should help a future implementation agent understand the boundary, evidence, and unresolved choices without turning the architecture runway into product implementation.
PKG-00 is intended to prevent later packages from making incompatible local choices about services, storage, diagnostics, GUI state, APIs, and acceptance gates.
Architecture guidance: prefer explicit contracts over package-local assumptions.
Architecture guidance: keep architecture language concrete enough for later implementation but abstract enough to avoid premature stack decisions.
Architecture guidance: use TBD when a decision needs human authority or later technical evaluation.
Architecture guidance: treat diagnostics, provenance, units, and data-boundary checks as cross-cutting architecture obligations.
Architecture guidance: preserve the distinction between mechanical calculation, user rule checking, and professional approval.
Decision handling: record a choice as TBD when no cited human ruling exists.
Decision handling: record a choice as PROPOSAL only when it is explicitly framed for review.
Decision handling: do not convert a proposed architecture option into an accepted decision inside this deliverable.
Decision handling: when a future package depends on this deliverable, cite the accepted architecture document or note the dependency is still awaiting human ruling.
Guardrail: do not copy or paraphrase protected standards tables, code text, or proprietary engineering values.
Guardrail: do not claim code compliance or professional approval.
Guardrail: use approved DAG-006 only for relationship context; do not infer lifecycle promotion, implementation readiness, or release acceptance from graph edges.
Guardrail: do not advance PKG-01 through PKG-12 from this deliverable.
Human-ruling queue: choose concrete repository layout and package manager after stack selection.
Human-ruling queue: approve dependency-direction rules before implementation planning.
The procedure purpose is to execute and review the deliverable-local architecture document kit without crossing the PKG-00 boundary.
Prerequisite: root bootstrap and governance documents have been read.
Prerequisite: execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7 is the current basis.
Prerequisite: coordination uses approved DAG-006 graph authority for relationship context, while deliverable-local _STATUS.md remains lifecycle authority.
Prerequisite: do not infer lifecycle promotion or implementation readiness from DAG context; human approval remains required for lifecycle changes.
Execution step: inventory the architecture layers named in SPEC and the PKG-00 scope items.
Execution step: map each layer to responsibilities, allowed dependencies, and forbidden bypasses.
Execution step: identify unresolved implementation-layout choices as TBD and route them to the ADR baseline.
Execution step: check the boundary map against the IP/data, unit-safety, and professional-authority invariants.
Execution step: prepare the module-boundary package for human architecture review.
Verification check: confirm the deliverable path is inside execution/PKG-00_Software Architecture Runway/.
Verification check: confirm _CONTEXT.md, _STATUS.md, _REFERENCES.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, and _SEMANTIC.md exist.
Verification check: confirm document-kit content maps to the scope items in _CONTEXT.md.
Verification check: confirm no PKG-01 through PKG-12 files are modified.
Verification check: confirm protected-content and professional-authority guardrails are stated.
Verification check: confirm unresolved decisions are visible as TBD.
Records to preserve for DEL-00-02 include Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, _SEMANTIC.md, _SEMANTIC_LENSING.md, _run_records/TASK_RUN_*.md, and _STATUS.md.

DEL-00-02 is ready for human architecture review when the document kit exists, semantic artifacts exist, lifecycle state is SEMANTIC_READY, and all unresolved architecture decisions are visible rather than silently resolved.
The specification governs only DEL-00-02 inside PKG-00 (Software Architecture Runway); it does not authorize implementation work in PKG-01 through PKG-12.
REQ-02-01: define intended responsibilities for GUI, application services, domain core, solver, rules, reports, adapters, storage, schemas, validation, and tests; evidence by acceptance review.
REQ-02-02: require dependencies to point inward toward domain contracts and not around unit, provenance, or data-boundary checks; evidence by acceptance review.
REQ-02-03: state that adapters and plugins may translate data but may not bypass governance, validation, or diagnostics contracts; evidence by acceptance review.
REQ-02-04: record TBD implementation-layout decisions without inventing repository specifics; evidence by acceptance review.
REQ-02-05: define review checks that detect package-local architecture drift before PKG-01 through PKG-12 proceed; evidence by human review.
Acceptance criterion: Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, and Procedure.md exist and cite the deliverable identity.
Acceptance criterion: all scope statements remain limited to PKG-00 architecture-runway work.
Acceptance criterion: TBD decisions are visible and routed to human ruling rather than silently selected.
Acceptance criterion: no implementation code, GUI screens, schemas, tests, or production package work are created.
Acceptance criterion: no protected standards/code data or proprietary engineering values are introduced.
Acceptance criterion: the semantic lens and lensing register exist for review and do not claim engineering authority.

Invariant OPS-K-IP-1: public artifacts must not contain protected standards text, tables, figures, copied formulas, material allowables, SIF/flexibility tables, protected dimensional tables, or proprietary commercial data.
Invariant OPS-K-DATA-2: missing solve-required or rule-check-required values remain explicit findings, never silent defaults.
Invariant OPS-K-AUTH-1: software and agents must not claim to certify, seal, approve, authenticate, or declare engineering code compliance for reliance.
Invariant OPS-K-MECH-1: global analysis architecture remains a 3D centerline/frame model; local FEA is a handoff path.
Invariant OPS-K-AGENT-1: unknown engineering or architecture facts become TBD.
Invariant OPS-K-AGENT-3: Type 2 execution stays within sealed deliverable scope.
Upstream authority for DEL-00-02 is SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md revision 0.7, the SCA-001/SCA-003/SCA-004 architecture-basis records, and approved DAG-006 graph authority.
Downstream consumers may use DEL-00-02 as AB-00-02 architecture-basis context only through sealed briefs and governed review/dispatch surfaces; this does not make PKG-00 ISSUED.
DAG-006 is approved graph authority for relationship context; lifecycle state remains deliverable-local, and PKG-00 architecture-basis rows are not implementation or release-readiness claims.
Human review must decide whether the architecture content is sufficient to support later PKG-01 through PKG-12 planning; SEMANTIC_READY means prepared for review, not accepted or issued.
